sources.citation: Brooks, Joseph Daniel. 2018. Realis and Irrealis: Chini Verb Morphology, Clause Chaining, and Discourse. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. xxi+345 pp. (eScholarship qt36s8s9t4)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing on Kominimung prosody (no data exist). Relevant passages: p. 70 (PDF 92): 'Two especially problematic language varieties are those labeled 'Kominimung' and 'Igana'. Z'graggen does not include a single transcribed word from either in his (1974) wordlist of the other Ramu languages, though in a subsequent work he alludes to "short wordlists" collected for Kominimung and Igana which he claims were "enough for classification" (1975:4).'; p. 72 (PDF 94): 'For Kominimung and Igana, also purported to be Ramu languages, no data are available.'; p. 78 (PDF 100): ''Goam' includes Chini as well…

sources.citation: Joshua Project. 2026. Language: Kominimung [xoi] (language profile page; alternate names Iski, Konminimung, Kuminimu, Okmaŋɨheŋgi; 'Bible Translation: Started'; 'No reported resources in this language'). Colorado Springs: Joshua Project. Accessed 2026-09-20.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing linguistic. Value as a pointer: 'Written: Unknown', 'Bible Translation: Started', no portions published, no GRN recordings, no resources — i.e. a translation programme (PBT/SIL, cf. Tousch's Iski word lists and Kwanga grammar) is active in the Iski cluster, so unpublished phonology notes may exist with the team, but nothing is archived or online.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: Guam River (Tamolan) family page, newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch (accessed 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Nothing on stress (the 'Historical phonology' section covers Proto-Guam River segments and root shapes only). States: 'Kominimung and Igana are listed as Tamolan languages in Z'graggen (1972, Laycock and Z'graggen 1975: 739-740) but no vocabularies were elicited.' Its Sources list (Z'graggen 1969/1971/1972/1974, O'Rear 1992, Brooks 2018, SIL survey vocabularies) contains no Kominimung data.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Kominimung language' (rev. 2026-04-07) and 'Tamolan languages' (rev. 2026-01-01)
sources.note: Nothing. 'Kominimung is a poorly known Ramu language'; 'Kominimung and Igana are said to also be Tamolan languages, but no data has been collected to establish that.' Cites only Ethnologue 18 (320 speakers, 2003) and Glottolog.

sources.citation: Barlow, Russell. 2023. A grammar of Ulwa (Papua New Guinea). Studies in Diversity Linguistics 372. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Nothing about Kominimung beyond its position in the Keram-Ramu family tree and name table (pp. 29-30: East Iski = Kominimung, Breri, Igana, Inapang, Chini). The phonology chapter concerns Ulwa only.

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul (ed.). 2009. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 16th edition, entry 'Kominimung [xoi]' (web edition, archived 2011-11-17); and Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue, 19th edition, entry 'Kominimung [xoi]' (archived 2016). Dallas: SIL International.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content. Full entry: population 320 (2003 SIL); Madang Province; status 6a Vigorous (19th ed.); classification Ramu-Lower Sepik > Ramu > Tamolan; 'Dialects: None known. Related to Romkun [rmk], Breri [brq], Igana [igg], Akrukay/Chini [afi], Inapang [mzu]'. No typology, writing or language-development line and no source named for the 2003 SIL figure.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & J. Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1 (PL C-38), 731-763. (ANU open-access scanned text, handle 1885/252975)
sources.note: Nothing; the chapter has no occurrence of 'stress', 'accent' or 'tone'. Kominimung appears once, in the list of Tamolan Family members (Midsivindi, Akrukay, Breri, Romkun, Kominimung, Igana).
sources.venue: New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The Languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. (ANU open-access scanned text; PDF at handle 1885/146484)
sources.note: Nothing on stress anywhere in the book (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing). p. 4: 'Short wordlists only were collected in B8 Dumun, A14 Bulgebi, A23 Mebu, M10 Kominimung and M11 Igana; they were however enough for a linguistic classification.' Kominimung (M10) is listed with 328 speakers in the villages Askunka and Kominimung.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and Typological Studies in Languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing for Kominimung: the name occurs once, as a village (pop. 151) of the Josephstaal Census Division in the area not yet surveyed ('Further fieldwork will have to demonstrate whether or not the languages in the unsurveyed area constitute links between the two sub phyla').

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record for Kominimung [komi1271] (Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank), incl. languoid JSON 'meds' field
sources.note: Nothing. Most-extensive-description ranking lists only two 'a wordlist or less' items: Tousch 2013 (Iski word lists, ms.) and Z'graggen 1975 (survey). No grammar, sketch or phonology exists for the language in Glottolog 5.3 (5.1 gave Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology).

sources.citation: Tousch, André. 2013. Iski word lists. Ms. 12 pp. (wordlists from Oguru, Lembubu, Kwanga, Misingi, Romakun, Yamu 2, Kominimung 1 and Igana villages)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only known primary data on Kominimung (Glottolog's most extensive description, a wordlist or less). A phonetic wordlist could carry stress marks on Kominimung forms, which would be the closest thing to a stress statement obtainable; Glottolog marks the file nosharefn (held in Hammarström's collection, not distributable), so access must go through the author (SIL-PNG) or Hammarström.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. (n.d., c. 1970s). Unpublished short survey wordlist(s) for Kominimung (M10) and Igana (M11), referred to at Z'graggen 1975: 4 as the only Kominimung material collected; presumably among Z'graggen's field notes/tapes (ANU Pacific Linguistics / Anthropos Institute papers)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Z'graggen 1975 p. 4 says short wordlists were collected at Kominimung and Usher notes the 1972 comparative wordlists omit it; the unpublished survey list is the only other primary transcription of the language and might carry stress marking. Existence attested only by that sentence; location not verified.

sources.citation: Hodgkinson, Barbara (consultant); Davra, Wenceslaus; Emhamka, Wesley; Gupu, Micheal; Knembi, David; Timbghi, Albert; Sraga, Justine (translators). 2001 (created 2001-08-16).
